I get such violent nightmares about the same place that I am afraid to fall asleep. 
Even if the dream starts simply, it quickly takes me to the same place, the same moment, playing out the same way every time.
I wake up in the middle of the night, drenched in sweat, heart hammering, completely convinced it just happened. I wake up dazed, and it takes minutes before I can locate myself in the present.
Even if I wake up from a nightmare, it feels so vivid that I feel I relieved it. 
My sleep has been broken and disturbed for months; even without a nightmare, I am somewhere in the dark all night. 
Many times, I have nightmares where the ending is different or worse. I wake up grieving something that didn't even happen that way.
column5: Recurring nightmares can really wear you down, and your sleep matters. A therapist — especially one trained in trauma — can help. Would you like me to help you find one?

I go blank sometimes, but I feel I am drowning, aware that there is a world above the surface, but unable to reach it.
My mom used to vigorously shake me to bring me back. She thought I was daydreaming, and I would return without knowing I had been gone.
When I am in a trance state, I can hear sounds from another room, like something distant and slightly unreal. But I cannot respond to them or make myself present.
If I have to point out, I feel it gets triggered by something bad, like a sound or smell, or even the way someone speaks. My system just takes me somewhere else without asking.
My children used to get scared when I would blank out, but now they know.  They wait patiently. They do not shake me, they just stay nearby.
